title: Tuple/Array Unification of Heterogeneous Concepts
pattern: Storing conceptually distinct attributes in a generic raw array or tuple simply because they are of the same type.
why_bad: The mapping knowledge (e.g., "index 0 is width, index 1 is height") is duplicated and scattered across all readers. Modifying the array structure forces a manual rewrite of all coordinate indexes, leading to silent index-shift corruption.
detection: Literal index lookups (e.g., `tuple.0`, `arr[1]`) on homogeneous data structures representing conceptually distinct domain properties.
counterexample: Homogeneous coordinates (e.g., $(x, y, z)$ coordinates) where coordinates are mathematically identical in behavior.
